clue.text: Losing heart in opera, become strongly attached

indicators.note: losing heart says the central letter of the opera's title drops out

parts.note: Faust is Gounod's opera

explanation.surface: Someone loses interest halfway through an opera yet ends up hooked on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing heart in' removes U, the middle letter of FAUST. 'become' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something held fast is firmly fixed, as in 'stuck fast'.

clue.text: Dreamy physicist taking wife for daughter

indicators.note: taking one thing for another signals a swap of letters

parts.note: Michael Faraday was the English physicist

explanation.surface: An absent-minded scientist marries instead of raising a child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking wife for daughter' replaces D with W in FARADAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A distant look is a dreamy, abstracted one.

clue.text: Extra pressure absorbed by litigant

indicators.note: absorbed by says the pressure goes inside the litigant

parts.note: a suer is one who brings a lawsuit
P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Additional strain is borne by the person bringing a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Super as a prefix or adjective means over and above, extra.

clue.text: So-called queen next to king is normal

indicators.note: so-called means 'called' in the sense of pronounced, so the word for normal is heard

parts.note: par is the normal standard, as in 'up to par'

explanation.surface: A consort seated beside the monarch is described as quite ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So-called' signals a sound-alike: PAR (normal) is pronounced the same as the surname. 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Catherine Parr was the last wife of Henry VIII, the queen at the king's side.

clue.text: Meeting requirements, being mature and flexible

parts.note: to age is to mature

indicators.note: flexible says the little word that follows can bend into a new order

explanation.surface: The conditions of a meeting call for experience and adaptability.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flexible' rearranges AND into NDA. 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A list of items to be dealt with at a meeting is what that gathering requires.

clue.text: Judge should allow no extremists to wreck peace

indicators.note: allowing no extremists means the end letters of the following word are dropped

parts.note: order is peace and calm, as in law and order

explanation.surface: A magistrate must keep radicals from disturbing public calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should allow no extremists' strips W and K from WRECK, leaving REC. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In England a part-time circuit judge in the Crown Court holds this title.

clue.text: Draw veil over couch to which one takes maiden

parts.note: a couch is a bed to lie on
I is the Roman numeral one
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: Someone draws a curtain round a sofa where a young woman is being led.
explanation.definitionFit: To dim or obscure something is to cast a veil over it.

clue.text: How one unfairly dismissed could be satisfied immediately?

definitions.text: How one unfairly dismissed could be satisfied immediately?

parts.words: How one unfairly dismissed could be satisfied immediately?
parts.note: a sacked worker would be content to get the job back, and the phrase also means at once in letters

explanation.definitionFit: A request for a reply at once uses this phrase, literally the next mail delivery.

clue.text: Too darned stormy — something refreshing needed

indicators.note: stormy suggests turbulence, so the two words are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: It's terribly muggy weather, and something to cool us down is required.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stormy' rearranges TOO DARNED.
explanation.definitionFit: A product applied to the armpits keeps a person fresh.

clue.text: Aquatic mammal's partner eating an eel for starters

indicators.note: eating says the partner takes in the next word

parts.note: a mate is a partner

indicators.note: for starters takes the first letter of the word eel

explanation.surface: A sea creature's companion is devouring an eel to begin its meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating' is a container signal, and 'for starters' takes an initial letter; the ''s' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea cow is a large plant-eating marine creature.

clue.text: In US, misrepresent a party project as threat to crop

parts.note: to colour a story is to misrepresent it, spelt the American way
a do is a party
to beetle is to project or overhang, as beetling brows

explanation.surface: Americans distort a political party's plans as a danger to farming.
explanation.definitionFit: This striped insect is a notorious pest that devastates potato crops.

clue.text: Carpet salesman has to travel

parts.note: a rep is a travelling sales representative
to rove is to travel about

explanation.surface: A rug seller has to go on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpet' looks like a floor covering, but here it is the verb meaning to tell someone off. 'has to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is British slang for to scold or rebuke them.

clue.text: No actor may be seen in such a film

definitions.text: No actor may be seen in such a film

parts.words: No actor may be seen in such a film
parts.note: a film made entirely of drawings has no live performers on screen

explanation.definitionFit: An animated film uses drawn characters, so no human performer appears on screen.

clue.text: Two commands in a meaningful sequence

parts.note: a word is a command, as in 'give the word'
an order is a command

explanation.surface: Instructions given one after the other in a sensible series.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Syntax arranges terms in a set arrangement so that a sentence makes sense.

clue.text: Swimmer last in heat — heavy defeat

indicators.note: last in picks the final letter of the word heat

parts.note: a rout is a crushing defeat

explanation.surface: A swimmer comes last in a qualifying race and is badly beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' sounds like a competitor in the race, but it is a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A fish is a swimmer, a crossword stock way of hiding any fish.

clue.text: Junior person never running counter?

parts.note: a subordinate who never goes against the boss's views always agrees

explanation.definitionFit: A sycophant who always agrees with superiors never runs counter to them.

clue.text: Under blanket, unable to move after fall

definitions.meaning: covered by a white layer, as a landscape after winter weather
stuck because of a heavy fall of flakes

explanation.definitionFit: A village cut off by heavy flakes is under a blanket and trapped there.

clue.text: Resistance, in end, ' seen to weaken

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: decease is death, one's end
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Opposition, when it finally comes, is seen to wane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts R inside DECEASE. 'seen to' is a link; the stray apostrophe is an OCR mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To lessen or diminish is to weaken.

clue.text: Get dispatched by the block, as notepaper may

definitions.meaning: be executed with an axe on the execution block

explanation.definitionFit: Executed by the axe, or as headed stationery is printed with a name at the top.

clue.text: Survey showing nothing right inside, nothing right outside

indicators.note: inside says the first pair of pieces goes within the second
outside says the second pair wraps around the first

parts.note: love is nothing as a score in tennis
O is the round figure zero, nothing
OK means all right
OK means all right

explanation.surface: A study reveals nothing is right anywhere, inside or out.
explanation.walkthrough: The same two words, 'nothing right', are read two different ways: once as short letters, once as a tennis score plus an abbreviation. 'showing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To survey something is to inspect or examine it.

clue.text: Representatives refuse to hold up badge

indicators.note: to hold means the refuse wraps around the next piece

parts.note: lees are dregs, the refuse left in wine

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a tag is a label or badge

explanation.surface: Delegates refuse to put up a lapel badge.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' signals reading from the bottom, and 'to hold' signals a container; 'refuse' looks like a verb but is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Papal envoys sent to act for the Pope are his emissaries.

clue.text: "Bow" rhymes with "row", possibly

parts.note: a deep bow, made of two halves, one rhyming with a quarrel and the other with rowing a boat

explanation.definitionFit: A Chinese-style low bow, touching the head to the ground, is a humble obeisance.

clue.text: Painful condition of' city overthrown in disaster

indicators.note: in tells us the city is placed within the disaster

parts.note: a wreck is a disaster

indicators.note: overthrown in a down clue means turned upside down, so read the city backwards

parts.note: NY is New York city

explanation.surface: A city's collapse into ruin is a painful state of affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overthrown' signals a reversal and 'in' a container. 'of' is a link; the stray apostrophe is an OCR mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A twisted neck held stiffly to one side, torticollis, is a painful complaint, also a bird's name.

clue.text: Two auxiliaries perform well

parts.note: be is an auxiliary verb
have is an auxiliary verb

explanation.surface: Two helpers do their job nicely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auxiliaries' sounds like helpers; it means auxiliary verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: To conduct oneself properly is to act well, to mind one's manners.

clue.text: Film actor built up to quite a pitch?

definitions.meaning: Clark, the Hollywood star of Gone with the Wind

definitions.text: built up to quite a pitch?
definitions.meaning: the triangular end wall of a house rises to a point under a pitched roof

explanation.definitionFit: Clark is the Hollywood star, and a house's triangular end wall rises to its roof's pitch.

clue.text: Model exam reply worked out

indicators.note: worked out tells us the letters of the two words are solved into a new order

explanation.surface: An ideal answer in a test, carefully thought through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked out' rearranges EXAM REPLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Model as an adjective means ideal, perfect, worthy of imitation.

clue.text: Calm down from a rage

parts.note: bate is British slang for a temper, as in 'in a bate'

explanation.surface: Settle down after a tantrum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To lessen or subside is to calm down, like a storm.

clue.text: Believed in faithful daughter — good man!

indicators.note: in tells us the good man is placed within the other pieces

parts.note: true means faithful, loyal
ST, saint, is a good man

explanation.surface: Someone trusted in a loyal daughter and praises a fine fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; ST for saint is a crossword convention for a good man.
explanation.definitionFit: To trust in someone is to have faith in them, to rely on them.

clue.text: Appease fool with talk of money to be earned

parts.note: an ass is a fool

indicators.note: talk of says we hear the word for pay rather than see it spelt

parts.note: a wage is money earned

explanation.surface: Calm an idiot by talking about how much they'll get paid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'talk of' means the word WAGE is pronounced, written UAGE to give the sound of the answer's ending. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To soothe or pacify someone is to appease them.

clue.text: Go gingerly with new driver in team

indicators.note: in tells us the driver is placed within the team

parts.note: a side is a team
L is the learner plate on a new driver's car

explanation.surface: A team proceeds cautiously after a novice joins at the wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link; L is the British learner-driver plate.
explanation.definitionFit: To move sideways, furtively or nervously, is to go gingerly.

clue.text: Where one takes only seconds to receive honourable discharge

definitions.text: Where one takes only seconds to receive honourable discharge

parts.words: Where one takes only seconds to receive honourable discharge
parts.note: an affair of honour attended by seconds, where a pistol shot is the discharge

explanation.definitionFit: A formal fight between two gentlemen, each attended by a second, was fought to settle honour.

clue.text: It's a privilege to make the coffee

definitions.meaning: a perquisite, a benefit of a job
to brew coffee in a percolator

explanation.definitionFit: A perquisite is a privilege, and a percolator brews coffee, shortened as a verb.
